from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Calculate using 3x3 matrix determinant.",
            "Organize components using unit vectors.",
            "Expand along the top row.",
            "Algorithm provides precise vector results.",
            "Practice with specific vector examples."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Computational Method: The Determinant", lecture_lines)
        
        # Matrix components
        matrix_str = r"\begin{vmatrix} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ a_x & a_y & a_z \\ b_x & b_y & b_z \end{vmatrix}"
        matrix = MathTex(matrix_str, font_size=36)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(matrix, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(matrix))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        # Highlighting row 1
        row1_highlight = matrix[0][0:9] # Indices for i, j, k
        self.play(row1_highlight.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        expansion = MathTex(r"= \mathbf{i}(a_y b_z - a_z b_y) - \mathbf{j}(a_x b_z - a_z b_x) + \mathbf{k}(a_x b_y - a_y b_x)", font_size=28)
        self.place_at_grid(expansion, 'D3', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(expansion))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        final_vec = MathTex(r"\mathbf{v} = \langle v_x, v_y, v_z \rangle", font_size=32, color="#FF0000")
        self.place_at_grid(final_vec, 'F2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(final_vec))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        example = MathTex(r"\mathbf{A} \times \mathbf{B} = \langle 1, 2, 3 \rangle \times \langle 4, 5, 6 \rangle", font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(example, 'F5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(example))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application: Torque", [
            "Torque is the cross product.",
            "Force applied to lever arm vectors.",
            "Determines the direction of rotation.",
            "Calculated using the cross product.",
            "Applied in real-world mechanical systems."
        ])
        
        # Define objects
        lever = Line(ORIGIN, 2*RIGHT, color=WHITE)
        force = Arrow(ORIGIN, 0.7*UP, color="#FF0000", buff=0)
        torque = Arrow(ORIGIN, 1*OUT, color="#00FF00", buff=0)
        
        lever_group = VGroup(lever, force).move_to(self.grid["C3"])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Create(lever))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        force.next_to(lever.get_end(), UP, buff=0)
        self.play(GrowArrow(force))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        # Rotation indication
        arc = Arc(start_angle=0, angle=PI/4, radius=0.5, color=YELLOW).next_to(lever.get_start(), RIGHT, buff=0)
        self.play(Create(arc))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        torque.move_to(lever.get_end())
        self.play(GrowArrow(torque))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFA500"))
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: Mastering the Cross Product: From 2D Geometry to 3D Space

sections.title: Prerequisites: Vectors and Planes
sections.content: Briefly define vectors as directed line segments with magnitude and direction. Remind students of the Right-Hand Rule (RHR) and the concept of an orthogonal vector (a vector perpendicular to a plane).
sections.example: Visualizing a flat sheet of paper (a plane) and a pencil standing straight up at 90 degrees to represent the normal vector.

sections.title: The 2D Pseudo-Cross Product
sections.content: Explain that while the cross product is strictly a 3D operation, in 2D we use a scalar 'perp product' (x1y2 - y1x2) to find the signed area of a parallelogram. It indicates orientation (clockwise vs counter-clockwise).
sections.example: A robotic arm on a 2D plane: calculating the 'perp product' of two joint vectors to determine if the arm needs to turn left or right to reach an object.

sections.title: The 3D Cross Product: Definition and Geometric Meaning
sections.content: Introduce the cross product as an operation resulting in a vector. Key property: The result is perpendicular to both input vectors. Its magnitude equals the area of the parallelogram formed by the two vectors.
sections.example: Animation of a butterfly flapping its wings: The cross product vector acts as the 'axis' of the wing's rotation, pointing directly outward.

sections.title: Computational Method: The Determinant
sections.content: Demonstrate the algebraic calculation using the 3x3 matrix determinant method. Show how the unit vectors i, j, and k organize the components of vectors A and B.
sections.example: Calculating the cross product of Vector A (1, 2, 3) and Vector B (4, 5, 6) using the 'expanding along the top row' technique.

sections.title: Real-World Application: Torque
sections.content: Conclude with the physics application of the cross product: Torque (τ = r × F). Explain how the cross product determines the direction of rotation when a force is applied to a lever arm.
sections.example: A mechanic using a wrench: the cross product of the wrench's length vector and the force vector applied to the handle shows exactly which way the bolt will rotate.
